meta.source: Meeting video transcripts (ASR, un-diarized); member attribution is name-based with per-position confidence.

cases.name: 115 Round Hill Road — Garage Second-Story Addition

timeline.summary: Mr. Gilbert presented a proposal to add a second story atop an existing detached garage at 115 Round Hill Road, designed to exactly match the main house's roofline, siding, color, and finishes, consistent with a prior second-story addition already completed on another part of the property. Board members confirmed the garage is detached (so zoning has no issue with the added height) and that all exterior finishes will match the existing house exactly. After brief confusion over some members not having received the plan materials electronically, the Board voiced unanimous support and a motion was made, seconded, and approved.

evidence.case: 115 Round Hill Road — Garage Second-Story Addition
evidence.evidence: Presiding over the meeting (welcomed the applicant, invited the presentation, and polled the board — 'I am fine. What about you guys?'), the chair voiced approval of the design before the motion carried unanimously. Attributed by role: Buhl-Tatka is the ARB's only chair across the Town's 2019-2025 records, so the presiding voice at this 2022 meeting is hers.

meetings.meetingSummary: This was a very brief North Castle Architectural Review Board meeting conducted over Zoom, consisting of a single agenda item: review of a proposed second-story addition atop a detached garage at 115 Round Hill Road, presented by the project's representative, Mr. Gilbert. The Board found the design consistent with the existing house and approved it within a few minutes of discussion. After the applicant left, members briefly discussed an unrelated administrative matter — artificial red poinsettia decorations still displayed on a town building, now more visible against the snow — and asked staff to check whether the town code addresses such decorations, closing with a note that the next meeting is scheduled for March 16.
meetings.durationNote: The recording begins mid-conversation (pre-meeting phone chatter caught on the live stream) and the ASR transcription was cut short after repeated silent audio chunks in the source recording, so total meeting length and a full attendance/quorum list could not be determined. Multiple members respond during deliberation (several distinct 'I'm fine' remarks before a motion was seconded), indicating quorum was met. The presiding voice is attributed to Chair Beata Buhl-Tatka by role (she is the ARB's only chair across the Town's 2019-2025 records).

meetings.attributionNote: No board member is identified by full name in the audio itself; attribution here uses the researched roster (Town records: Beata Buhl-Tatka chair, Susan Geffen, Christopher Tuzzo, John Scarlato, plus a fifth seat held by Angelo Monaco earlier and Mel Orellana later — its occupant on this exact date is unconfirmed). The presiding voice is attributed to Chair Buhl-Tatka at medium confidence by role; the remaining deliberation voices ('I'm okay with what I saw,' 'I'm fine,' 'I second it') could not be tied to specific members and were left unattributed. Names actually heard: 'Mr. Gilbert' (the applicant's project representative for 115 Round Hill Road, once addressed as 'John' — likely John Gilbert); 'Lori' (mentioned in passing — Lori J. Zawacki, the Board Secretary per the Town's ARB agendas); and a 'John' addressed in the closing discussion about artificial decorations on a town building, who says he was not 'in the office' that day and will follow up on the town code — plausibly board member John Scarlato (an architect with a local office), but possibly Town staff, so this remark is deliberately left unattributed rather than guessed.
